newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice futures end down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice futures end down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down in slow trading on Wednesday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The only traded October contract ended at 2,300 yuan ($276) per tonne, losing 12 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 2,280 and hit a high of 2,306.

Traders said liquidation of long-term positions by retail investors pushed the contract down. "Long liquidation by retail investors was responsible for today's falls but the contract found support at the 2,300-yuan level," a trader said.
"Most retail investors did not want to build long positions because they were willing to take physical goods," a second trader said.
Traders said room for further falls would be limited due to higher spot prices in Shanghai, which are currently around 2,400 yuan per tonne.
